title: Piperade Basque
subtitle: Basque stewed peppers and tomatoes with eggs stirred through
excerpt: Red and green peppers, onion, and tomatoes are cooked low and slow until they collapse into a soft, sweet stew. Eggs are stirred in at the end and cooked gently until just set. A Basque dish that sits somewhere between a sauce and a supper.
sourceNotes: Basque Country classic from the Pyrenees border region. Synthesised from the traditional Labourdine preparation.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the pepper and tomato base up to 2 days ahead. Reheat gently and stir in the eggs just before serving.

content.text: Piperade needs slow cooking to work. The peppers must go completely soft before the tomatoes go in. The eggs are added off the heat and stirred to a very loose, creamy consistency. Do not let them scramble.
Warm the olive oil in the wide frying pan over a low heat. Add the onions and a pinch of salt. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft and starting to turn pale gold.
Add the sliced peppers and the chilli if using. Cook over a low to medium heat for 15 minutes until the peppers are completely soft. Stir every few minutes.
Add the garlic, thyme, and bay leaves. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add the tinned tomatoes. Season with salt and pepper. Stir and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes until the mixture thickens and most of the liquid has gone.
Remove the thyme sprigs and bay leaves. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Reduce the heat to very low. Pour the beaten eggs over the pepper mixture. Stir gently and continuously with a wooden spoon for 2 to 3 minutes.
Stop while the eggs are still very soft and slightly underdone. They will finish in the residual heat. Serve straight from the pan with bread.

items.symptom: The eggs have scrambled and separated from the peppers.
items.cause: The heat was too high when the eggs were added.
items.fix: The heat must be very low before the eggs go in. Stir gently and pull the pan off the heat as soon as the eggs are barely set.

items.symptom: The base is watery even after 10 minutes of simmering.
items.cause: The peppers released a lot of liquid and the heat was not high enough to reduce it.
items.fix: Simmer uncovered for 5 minutes more on a medium heat before adding the eggs.

items.symptom: The pepper base tastes sweet but flat.
items.cause: No acid to balance the natural sweetness of the peppers.
items.fix: Add a small splash of sherry vinegar or white wine vinegar and stir through before adding the eggs.
